claims.text: Developing a machine-learning potential can help produce noble-metal-based HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
A machine-learning potential can simulate the formation of HEAs.
A machine-learning potential can simulate properties of HEAs.
Machine-learning simulation can accelerate the discovery of new HEA materials.
The resulting discovered materials will have unique properties.
The machine-learning potential is the structural mediator for producing the nanoframeworks.
The proposed mechanism uses machine-learning algorithms to simulate HEA formation and properties.
The proposed mechanism relies on large datasets.
The intervention will produce NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Arc melting, mechanical alloying, and spark plasma sintering are current HEA-production methods forming the baseline.
Development of the potential is limited by the availability of large datasets.
Development of the potential is limited by computational-resource availability.
It is uncertain whether the potential can accurately predict NM-HEA behavior.
It is uncertain whether the method is scalable to large-scale industrial applications.
A comparison with traditionally produced NM-HEAs using microstructural, mechanical, and thermal measurements is proposed.
The hypothesis is to be rejected if materials attributed to the machine-learning potential do not differ significantly from traditionally produced materials.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mechanism define the machine-learning potential as a computational simulation tool, while the outcome and experiment refer to NM-HEAs being physically produced using that potential. No fabrication intervention connecting simulation to physical nanoframework production is specified.
